arxiv-2203-02303.description: Abstract The reconstruction of event-level information, such as the direction or energy of a neutrino interacting in IceCube DeepCore, is a crucial ingredient to many physics analyses. Algorithms to extract this high level information from the detector’s raw data have been successfully developed and used for high energy events.

arxiv-2302-04640.title: Prefixes of the Fibonacci word
arxiv-2302-04640.creator: Jeffrey Shallit
arxiv-2302-04640.description: Abstract Mignosi, Restivo, and Salemi (1998) proved that for all ϵ > 0 \epsilon>0 there exists an integer N N such that all prefixes of the Fibonacci word of length ≥ N \geq N contain a suffix of exponent α 2 − ϵ \alpha^{2}-\epsilon , where α = ( 1 + 5 ) / 2 \alpha=(1+\sqrt{5})/2 is the golden ratio.

arxiv-2303-04090.title: Assessment of error variation in high-fidelity two-qubit gates in silicon
arxiv-2303-04090.creator: Tuomo Tanttu, Wee Han Lim, Jonathan Y. Huang, Nard Dumoulin Stuyck, Will Gilbert, Rocky Y. Su, MengKe Feng, Jesus D. Cifuentes, Amanda E. Seedhouse, Stefan K. Seritan, Corey I. Ostrove, Kenneth M. Rudinger, Ross C. C. Leon, Wister Huang, Christopher C. Escott, Kohei M. Itoh, Nikolay V. Abrosimov, Ha
arxiv-2303-04090.description: Abstract Achieving high-fidelity entangling operations between qubits consistently is essential for the performance of multi-qubit systems and is a crucial factor in achieving fault-tolerant quantum processors. Solid-state platforms are particularly exposed to errors due to materials-induced variability between qubits, which leads to performance inconsistencies. Here we study the errors in a spin qubit processor, tying them to their physical origins.

arxiv-2303-17920.title: Hamel equations and quasivelocities for nonholonomic systems with inequality constraints
arxiv-2303-17920.creator: Alexandre Anahory Simoes, Leonardo Colombo
arxiv-2303-17920.description: Abstract In this paper we derive Hamel equations for the motion of nonholonomic systems subject to inequality constraints in quasivelocities. As examples, the vertical rolling disk hitting a wall and the Chaplygin sleigh with a knife edge constraint hitting a circular table are shown to illustrate the theoretical results.

arxiv-2412-04785.title: Differentially Private Random Feature Model
arxiv-2412-04785.creator: Chunyang Liao, Deanna Needell, Hayden Schaeffer, Alexander Xue
arxiv-2412-04785.description: Abstract Designing privacy-preserving machine learning algorithms has received great attention in recent years, especially in the setting when the data contains sensitive information. Differential privacy (DP) is a widely used mechanism for data analysis with privacy guarantees. In this paper, we produce a differentially private random feature model.

arxiv-2412-19170.title: Fluid-particle interactions and fluctuation-dissipation relations III - Correlated fluctuations, regularity and added mass
arxiv-2412-19170.creator: Massimiliano Giona, Giuseppe Procopio, Chiara Pezzotti
arxiv-2412-19170.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Massimiliano Giona, Giuseppe Procopio, Chiara Pezzotti. The fluctuation-dissipation theory is grounded on the Langevin condition expressing the local independence between the thermal force and the particle velocity history. Upon hydrodynamic grounds, it is reasonable to relax this condition in order to account for the correlated fluid fluctuations, especially in the case of liquids, consistently with the inclusion of acoustic effects and with the finite speed of propagation of internal shear stresses.

arxiv-2502-05331.title: Fine-Tuned LLMs are “Time Capsules” for Tracking Societal Bias Through Books
arxiv-2502-05331.creator: Sangmitra Madhusudan, Robert Morabito, Skye Reid, Nikta Gohari Sadr, and Ali Emami
arxiv-2502-05331.description: Abstract Books, while often rich in cultural insights, can also mirror societal biases of their eras—biases that Large Language Models (LLMs) may learn and perpetuate during training. We introduce a novel method to trace and quantify these biases using fine-tuned LLMs. We develop BookPAGE , a corpus comprising 593 fictional books across seven decades (1950-2019), to track bias evolution.

arxiv-2505-12747.title: Temporal SU(1,1) Interferometer with Broadband Squeezed Light Injection
arxiv-2505-12747.creator: Zepeng Liu 1, Tianyu Liu 1, Hongmei Ma 2, Chun-Hua Yuan 1
arxiv-2505-12747.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Zepeng Liu 1, Tianyu Liu 1, Hongmei Ma 2, Chun-Hua Yuan 1. Temporal optics has attracted much attention due to its ability for lossless stretching of ultrafast temporal pulses. At the same time, spatial SU(1,1) interferometers have been widely used because of their high sensitivity to phase changes. On this basis, we studied a temporal SU(1,1) interferometer based on a temporal Fourier transform system and injected broadband squeezing light into the interferometer for research.

arxiv-2512-15162.creator: Rui-Zhi Li, Jirong Mao, Yuan-Pei Yang, Bo-Ting Wang, Fei-Fan Song, Yu-Xin Xin, Jin-Ming Bai
arxiv-2512-15162.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Rui-Zhi Li, Jirong Mao, Yuan-Pei Yang, Bo-Ting Wang, Fei-Fan Song, Yu-Xin Xin, Jin-Ming Bai. Long-duration gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are believed to occur in star-forming regions. The multiwavelength follow-up observations of the early afterglow of GRB 240825A provided insights into the evolution of the optical-to-X-ray spectral feature of the afterglow. We comprehensively investigate the evolution of X-ray spectral properties through time-resolved spectral analysis and calculate optical darkness ( β OX \beta_{\mathrm{OX}} ) to reveal the physical properties of the afterglow.

pmc-13212382.creator: Maarten V. de Hoop, Matti Lassas, Jinpeng Lu, Lauri Oksanen, Ziyao Zhao
pmc-13212382.description: We study the inverse problem of determining a Signorini obstacle from boundary measurements for the isotropic elasticity system. We prove that the obstacle can be uniquely determined by a single measurement of displacement and normal stress for the Signorini problem on an open subset of the boundary up to a natural obstruction.

pmc-13244965.title: From scat to seedling: seasonal variation in seed deposition and emergence by chacma baboons (Papio ursinus) in a semi-arid South African savanna
pmc-13244965.creator: Mpoko Belly Malatji, Sellina Ennie Nkosi
pmc-13244965.description: Seed dispersal by primates is a key ecological process, yet research remains comparatively limited in semi-arid savannas. This study investigates the seasonal variation in scat-derived seed deposition and emergence patterns of chacma baboons (Papio ursinus) and their potential role as seed dispersers in Suikerbosrand Nature Reserve, South Africa.
